title: feat: prerelease support in compare() and satisfies()
description:
Adds prerelease support (SemVer 2.0.0 §9 and §11).

- parse() now returns `prerelease: string[]`.
- compare() orders a prerelease below the release with the same major.minor.patch; numeric identifiers compare numerically.
- satisfies(): prerelease versions are excluded from ranges unless the range names the same major.minor.patch with a prerelease of its own (npm semver behaviour), e.g. satisfies('1.3.0-beta.1', '^1.2.0') === false.

No behaviour change intended for release versions.

charges.claim: compare() no longer orders versions that differ only in the patch component: the loop stops at MAIN.length - 1, so compare('1.2.3', '1.2.4') returns 0.
satisfies() now rejects prerelease versions that the range covers: satisfies('1.3.0-beta.1', '^1.2.0') went from true to false.
The rewritten SEMVER regex drops support for a leading 'v', so parse('v1.2.3') now throws.
comparePrerelease() accepts numeric identifiers with leading zeros ('01'), which SemVer 2.0.0 §9 forbids; it should throw.
satisfies() now parses the version twice per call, a measurable slowdown on hot range checks.

rebuttals.argument: Conceded. The witness uses only release versions, which the PR description says should be unaffected. Base returns -1 for compare('1.2.3', '1.2.4'); head returns 0 because the loop bound MAIN.length - 1 stops before 'patch'. Nothing in the PR suggests this is intended.

Not a bug. The PR description says prerelease versions are excluded from ranges unless the range names the same major.minor.patch with a prerelease, and gives this exact example: satisfies('1.3.0-beta.1', '^1.2.0') === false. The comment at src/range.js:7-8 says the same, and it matches npm semver, where semver.satisfies('1.3.0-beta.1', '^1.2.0') is false. The witness asserts the pre-PR contract that this PR deliberately replaces.

rulings.reason: Admissible evidence on release-only inputs, and the defense concedes. compare() skips the patch component (src/compare.js:28), so 1.2.3 and 1.2.4 compare as equal; sorting and every range check that depends on patch order are affected. Regression introduced by this PR.

The witness reproduces a real behaviour change, but it is the change the PR announces and it matches npm semver's prerelease rule. The witness encodes the superseded contract; intentional, documented behaviour is not a defect.
Inadmissible: the witness passes on head 3/3. Dismissed without a hearing.
Inadmissible: the witness errors on base 3/3, so it cannot demonstrate a regression. Dismissed without a hearing.
Inadmissible: the witness is flaky on head (2 of 3 runs failed); a timing threshold is not evidence. Dismissed without a hearing.

remedy.explanation: compare() stops one component early: the loop bound MAIN.length - 1 skips 'patch', so versions that differ only in patch compare equal. The fix restores the full bound; prerelease ordering still applies only when major, minor and patch are equal. Attempt 1 also rewrote comparePrerelease() and failed the existing suite; attempt 2 changes only the loop bound.
